 # Background: The Lanczos iteration is an iterative method for constructing an orthonormal basis for the Krylov subspace K_m(A, b) = span{b, Ab, A^2b, ..., A^{m-1}b} of a symmetric matrix A. It uses a three-term recurrence relation to generate vectors q_j such that the matrix Q = [q_1, q_2, ..., q_{m+1}] has orthonormal columns. The algorithm computes alpha_j = q_j^T * A * q_j and beta_j = ||v_j||, where v_j = A * q_j - alpha_j * q_j - beta_{j-1} * q_{j-1}. To maintain numerical stability against floating-point errors, explicit re-orthogonalization is often employed. def lanczos(A, b, m): '''Inputs: A : Matrix, 2d array of arbitrary size M * M b : Vector, 1d array of arbitrary size M * 1 m : integer, m < M Outputs: Q : Matrix, 2d array of size M*(m+1) ''' M = A.shape[0] Q = np.zeros((M, m + 1)) # Normalize initial vector q = b / np.linalg.norm(b) Q[:, 0] = q beta = 0 q_prev = np.zeros(M) for j in range(m): v = A @ Q[:, j] alpha = np.dot(Q[:, j], v) v = v - alpha * Q[:, j] - beta * q_prev # Re-orthogonalization to maintain stability for i in range(j + 1): v -= np.dot(Q[:, i], v) * Q[:, i] beta = np.linalg.norm(v) if beta < 1e-12: break q_prev = Q[:, j] Q[:, j + 1] = v / beta return Q

The process involves iteratively applying the matrix A to the current vector, orthogonalizing against the previous two vectors (due to the three-term recurrence relation for symmetric matrices), and normalizing the result.

def lanczos(A, b, m):
    '''Inputs:
    A : Matrix, 2d array of arbitrary size M * M
    b : Vector, 1d array of arbitrary size M * 1
    m : integer, m < M
    Outputs:
    Q : Matrix, 2d array of size M*(m+1)
    '''
    M = A.shape[0]

        beta[j] = np.linalg.norm(v)
        
        if beta[j] < 1e-12:
            break
            
        Q[:, j+1] = v / beta[j]
        
    return Q

# Background: The Lanczos iteration is an algorithm used to compute the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a large, sparse symmetric matrix. It constructs an orthonormal basis for the Krylov subspace K_m(A, b) = span{b, Ab, A^2b, ..., A^{m-1}b}. The process uses a three-term recurrence relation to generate the basis vectors (Lanczos vectors), which form the columns of the matrix Q. The algorithm maintains orthogonality through the Gram-Schmidt process implicitly via the recurrence, though in practice, re-orthogonalization may be needed to combat numerical instability.

def lanczos(A, b, m):
    '''Inputs:
    A : Matrix, 2d array of arbitrary size M * M
    b : Vector, 1d array of arbitrary size M * 1
    m : integer, m < M
    Outputs:
    Q : Matrix, 2d array of size M*(m+1)
    '''
    M = A.shape[0]
    Q = np.zeros((M, m + 1))
    alpha = np.zeros(m)
    beta = np.zeros(m)

    # Normalize initial vector
    q = b / np.linalg.norm(b)
    Q[:, 0] = q

    for j in range(m):
        v = A @ Q[:, j]
        if j > 0:
            v -= beta[j-1] * Q[:, j-1]
        
        alpha[j] = np.dot(Q[:, j], v)
        v -= alpha[j] * Q[:, j]
        
        # Re-orthogonalization (optional but recommended for stability)
        for k in range(j + 1):
            v -= np.dot(Q[:, k], v) * Q[:, k]
            
        beta[j] = np.linalg.norm(v)
        
        if beta[j] < 1e-12:
            break
            
        Q[:, j+1] = v / beta[j]
        
    return Q
